oss_reference.repo: lssfau/lbmpy (+ its waLBerla python binding lbmpy_walberla, local checkout /tmp/lbmpy_src and /tmp/walberla)
oss_reference.approach: MPI ghost-layer exchange driven by a generated PackInfo: per communication direction only the populations that actually cross that face are packed/unpacked (packDirection / unpackDirection, sized by getSizeOfPackedCellInterval), the pack and unpack are generated kernels fused into one pass per direction, and in-place streaming patterns get separate Even/Odd PackInfos
sources_of_record: lbmpy_walberla/packinfo.py :: generate_lb_pack_info (class_name+'Even'/'Odd' per Timestep; spec[(comm_dir,)] = write accesses of set(_extend_dir(comm_dir)) & set(stencil))

lbmpy_walberla/templates/PackingKernels.tmpl.h :: packAll/unpackAll, packDirection/unpackDirection, getSizeOfPackedCellInterval (docstring: 'if dir == N, the pdfs streaming in directions NW, N, NE are packed')
oss_reference.execution_limit: no mpi4py / no MPI implementation in this image (mpi4py MISSING) and no GPU; the OSS semantics are therefore transplanted onto TensorLBM's real torch.distributed/gloo point-to-point transport and executed, not the OSS binaries. Recorded as a comparison limit, not upgraded.

decision: Does transplanting lbmpy/waLBerla's direction-selective, kernel-fused MPI PackInfo ghost exchange into TensorLBM's x-slab D3Q19 transport (a) reproduce the monolithic solution bit-exactly, (b) keep the Taylor-Green vortex accuracy inside the owner 15% band, and (c) cut per-step exchange bytes by the predeclared stencil-derived factor Q/n_cross = 19/5 = 3.8x versus the shipped full-19-plane exchange?

alternatives.A_serial: TensorLBM monolithic single-buffer D3Q19 pull stream over the whole (19,n,n,n) lattice, periodic in x,y,z by torch.roll -- physical reference for the analytic comparison and for arm identity
alternatives.A_ship: shipped tensorlbm.multi_gpu.D3Q19GlooTransport.step semantics: collide, isend/irecv the FULL 19-population boundary planes, waitall, unpack all 19 channels, then pull stream (exchange replicated in-module so the ablation shares one code path; the replica is cross-checked against the shipped class in tests)
alternatives.A_fused: OSS PackInfo transplant: per face only the crossing populations (cx=+1 to the right neighbour, cx=-1 to the left neighbour; 5 of 19 for D3Q19) are packed into contiguous direction-sized buffers, exchanged, and unpacked in one fused index-write into the ghost plane
alternatives.A_fused_persistent: A_fused with a preallocated persistent padded buffer reused across steps (ablation of the buffer-allocation factor, isolating bytes from allocation)
alternatives.A_ship_persistent: A_ship with the persistent padded buffer (2x2 ablation: {selective,full-19} x {alloc,persistent})

hypothesis.H1_semantics: the crossing-population derivation transcribed from lbmpy's _extend_dir is identical to the OSS function's output intersected with the D3Q19 stencil for all 26 communication directions, and pack/unpack are a lossless permutation of exactly those entries
hypothesis.H2_identity: every decomposed arm reproduces the monolithic field bit-exactly (max|df| == 0.0) in float64 and float32, because decomposition may only change data movement, never arithmetic
hypothesis.H3_physics: TGV at 64^3 reaches the analytic solution inside the owner 15% band and inside the 5% engineering target
hypothesis.H4_bytes: selective exchange moves exactly n_cross/Q = 5/19 = 0.2632 of the shipped wire bytes per face per step
falsifiers: H1 fails if any communication direction's crossing set differs from lbmpy's, or if unpacked ghost entries differ from the packed source anywhere (>= 1 bit)
H2 fails if any arm's max|df| is nonzero
H4 fails if the measured byte ratio deviates from 5/19

metrics.identity_max_abs: max|f_arm - f_serial| over the assembled owned field after the predeclared step count (float64 and float32 runs)
metrics.tgv_rel_l2: ||u_num - u_analytic||_2 / ||u_analytic||_2 over the three velocity components on the full domain at t_end
metrics.wire_bytes_per_face_step: sum of numel*element_size over the two send and two receive buffers of one step, averaged per face
metrics.exchange_ms: wall time of the exchange call accumulated over the timed steps / timed steps
metrics.step_ms: wall time of collide+exchange+stream per step, median over the timed steps

unit_of_analysis: one completed simulation arm at a fixed (n, rank count, dtype, tau, U0, step count)

baseline_control.physical_baseline: the same code's monolithic run (A_serial) and the TGV analytic solution u = U0 sin(kx) cos(ky) cos(kz) e^{-2 nu k^2 t}, v = -U0 cos(kx) sin(ky) cos(kz) e^{-2 nu k^2 t}, w = 0, k = 2 pi / n
baseline_control.representation_control: A_ship vs A_fused -- collision, streaming, geometry, dtype and step count identical; the only changed variable is the packed population set (plus the buffer-allocation ablation)
baseline_control.oss_control: the crossing-population set is machine-compared against lbmpy._extend_dir (the OSS function itself), not against a hand-written table

predeclared_thresholds.interpretation: the 15% band is the owner physics band and applies to tgv_rel_l2; the identity comparison uses an exact-zero threshold because a data-movement change has no legitimate numerical freedom; the byte ratio has no tolerance because it is an integer count
predeclared_thresholds.convergence_rule: the TGV error is reported at n=32 and n=64; a metric is declared resolution-converged when the error does not grow and the amplitude ratio moves toward 1; no arm is re-tuned after the KPIs are seen
predeclared_thresholds.sensitivity_rule: rank count 2 vs 4 at fixed n=64 (fixed global work, growing comm surface) and n=32 vs n=64 at fixed 2 ranks; both are predeclared sensitivity points
predeclared_thresholds.stability_rule: a run with a non-finite population, rho outside [0.9,1.1] or Ma = U0*sqrt(3) > 0.2 is declared failed and reported, never tuned away

stopping_rule: every arm runs the step count fixed here (400 steps n=64, 200 steps n=32) and stops early only on non-finite state; no arm is extended after looking at KPIs. Wall-clock budget 600 s per arm; anything above that moves to the cluster queue.

environment.transport: torch.distributed gloo, point-to-point isend/irecv over localhost, one process per rank, torch.set_num_threads(1) per rank
